behavior: Preserves exact pinned Standard_RangeError, Standard_TypeMismatch, Standard_OutOfRange and Standard_DimensionMismatch message strings instead of substituting generic Rust shape/index text for native failures. Existing Rust-only shape/alignment/overflow restrictions remain separate.

Constructor messages distinguish zero stride, unsigned zero size, signed nonpositive length and empty external buffer. Unsigned construction validates stride before count; signed construction delegates through checkedSize before checking stride. Resize uses its own unsigned zero-size message and the shared native signed-length message.

Typed signed access rejects negative indices before testing payload width. Nonnegative and unsigned typed access test exact/prefix width first, then delegate index validation to lowercase value/changeValue. The resulting upper/lowercase overload names are observable and now match native payloads.

Data and ChangeData type errors retain their exact method names. Init goes through ChangeData and therefore reports ChangeData on type mismatch. Assign stride/count mismatches use the native shared arrays-have-different-size payload.

All native-compatible error sites use Failure::with_message, preserving native default stack capture.48 default rows compare type, exact message and empty-stack flag;4 isolated stack-enabled rows compare nonempty capture flags for type, range, dimension and index errors. No stack frame addresses or exact frame count are claimed identical.

Output-parameter failure paths leave both initialized destination values unchanged. Shared checked signed-index/type/range helpers preserve overload precedence, and resized_storage extraction keeps the parent candidate allocation/copy behavior unchanged.

The four original OCCT runtime names join both final normal and strict Miri logs. Six AliasedArray integration targets run normally (24 tests); Miri runs23 with the positive-stack FFI test explicitly excluded. Parent initial red/green/normal/Miri/native logs are retained as historical evidence; final logs after helper splits are authoritative.
limitations: All bindings remain partial. Alignment is the current Rust owned-buffer/default-native alignment domain; arbitrary native MyAlignSize specializations and externally misaligned typed references are not completed.
Rust owned bytes are zero initialized where native new/grown bytes are indeterminate. Tests do not claim native uninitialized reads or full byte-for-byte allocation behavior.

Native allocation failures, resize discard-before-allocation failure state, raw allocation ABI and overflow/resource-exhaustion policies remain actionable gaps. This batch only corrects the tested exception sites before those operations.

Native move/Move retains a source pointer/range with changed ownership; current Rust alias/move representation does not cover all of that behavior. Overlapping borrowed aliases, mutable access through native const wrappers and unrestricted raw C++ payloads remain outside this safe Pod/slice representation.
ArrayValue requires bytemuck::Pod. C++ non-Pod payloads and arbitrary user-defined assignment behavior are not supported by these existing adapters.

Signed borrowed-buffer constructor and First/Last convenience exception branches are not newly claimed as exact-message native probes here; scoped44 bindings cover the directly exercised families and their checked helper declarations.

Positive stack capture is tested by presence only in separate native and Rust processes, using each runtime stack implementation. Strict Miri does not establish real libc stack capture; underlying linked TKernel is prebuilt and not itself rebuilt with UBSan.
validation_scope: Completed the coordinating agent's unchanged production/test/native candidate after its resize/C++ helper splits. Final six-target normal24, strictMiri23, strict Clippy,fmt,docs,compiler and52 native diagnostic rows pass; four original legacy tests retain their prior credit.44 exact native AST IDs bind28 unique public Rust method bodies. No shared parity ledger changes.
